We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“It was a big ask in terms of coming back from America on Monday and you’ve got to give the lads credit for going close. There were a lot of positives in the performance.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupMiddlesbroughWrexhammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Panthers rally past Cardinals behind undrafted rookie QB in NFL preseason opener | NFL | The Guardian
description: Haynes King rushed for the winning score as time expired to give Carolina a 33-30 victory over Arizona in the Hall of Fame game to kick of the NFL preseason
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Haynes King rushed for the winning score as time expired to give Carolina a 33-30 victory over Arizona in the Hall of Fame game to kick of the NFL preseason
Content: Carolina Panthers tight end Ja'tavion Sanders (center) celebrates with quarterback Haynes King (16) after King scored a touchdown on the last play of the game on Thursday in Canton, Ohio.Photograph: David Richard/APView image in fullscreenCarolina Panthers tight end Ja'tavion Sanders (center) celebrates with quarterback Haynes King (16) after King scored a touchdown on the last play of the game on Thursday in Canton, Ohio.Photograph: David Richard/APNFLPanthers rally past Cardinals behind undrafted rookie QB in NFL preseason openerRookie Haynes King caps comeback in 33-30 winArizona’s Carson Beck also impresses on debutHall of Fame game opens 2026 NFL preseasonAssociated PressFri 7 Aug 2026 07.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMaybe a team should’ve drafted Haynes King.The rookie quarterback ran in from the five-yard line on the final play to give theCarolina Panthersa 33-30 victory over the Arizona Cardinals in the Hall of Fame game that kicked off the NFL preseason on Thursday night.King, who was the Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year last season at Georgia Tech, was 21 of 34 for 180 yards and two touchdowns. He ran for 39 yards and the winning score.Washington Commanders to sign four-time Pro Bowl receiver Stefon DiggsRead more“Well, that was a lot of fun. Just the back and forth of it. Just a really good game,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. “The guys were resilient and finish is what we preach as a team. We practice for these situations, end of half, end of game. ... Haynes did a fantastic job, just keeping the play alive, doing whatever he had to do, run it, throw it. Really proud of the group.”Carson Beck also had an impressive debut for Arizona.After Beck left, Kedon Slovis tossed a one-yard TD pass to Bryson Green with 1:55 remaining to give the Cardinals a 30-27 lead.But King rallied the Panthers on a night when both teams didn’t play their starters. Bryce Young was King’s biggest cheerleader on the sideline.King’s four-yard TD pass to Anthony Tyus III in the opening minute of the fourth quarter put Carolina ahead 24-20. King threw a 15-yard TD pass Ja’seem Reed in the second quarter. He had a 26-yard run on third-and-14 to keep the final drive going.“These are things that he did throughout his career,” Canales said of King. “The bottom line is move the chains.”Both teams gave their backups and reserves opportunities to shine.Beck, Slovis and King took advantage.Beck, a third-round pick from Miami, completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and one touchdown. After leading the Hurricanes to the national championship game – a loss to Fernando Mendoza and Indiana – Beck wasn’t overwhelmed by the national stage.“It was a cool environment and for him to just kind of, it’s just another game and that’s the way he took it and he’s been in big ones and that’s how his mindset works,” rookie Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said.Slovis was 9 of 10 for 106 yards.Veteran Jacoby Brissett is the Cardinals’ starter and their backup is journeyman Gardner Minshew. But expectations are low for Arizona in a division that includes the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, Rams and 49ers.So Beck may get a chance to play at some point if he develops under LaFleur. Canales raved about what he saw from the opposing sideline.“He operated like a professional. He looked fantastic,” Canales said. “He was accurate. He was on time. Our rush was decent. He got the ball out, threw some really beautiful passes down the field, up the sideline on some double moves, over the middle, to keep the drive alive in some third-down situations, so tip my hat to him.”King is expected to be Carolina’s No 3 QB behind Young and veteran Kenny Pickett.The Panthers won the NFC South last season at 8-9 and lost to the Rams in a wildcard game.Pickett started and was 8 of 11 for 62 yards before King replaced him.Beck completed all six of his passes on a 98-yard touchdown drive that included a 35-yard strike to Jalen Brooks on third-and-7 from Arizona’s seven.He threw a perfect deep ball to Brooks for a 49-yard gain and finished that drive with a five-yard TD pass to Simi Fehoko.Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love, the No 3 overall pick in the draft, sat out even though he hoped to persuade LaFleur to let him play.Quarterback Drew Brees, running back Roger Craig, kicker Adam Vinatieri, wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald and linebacker Luke Kuechly make up the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026.Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin made his first appearance with the NBC broadcast crew. Tomlin left Pittsburgh after 19 seasons and became the lead studio analyst for Football Night in America.Brissett and All-Pro tight end Trey McBride stopped by the Pro Football Hall of Fame Museum to see their jerseys displayed for breaking records last season. McBride set anNFLrecord for receptions by a tight end in a season with 126. Brissett set a record for completions in a game with 47 against San Francisco last 16 November.Cardinals players wore red T-shirts with Larry Fitzgerald’s No 11 in warmups and on the sideline.“It’s a great feeling to know your organization stands behind you,” Fitzgerald said. “I’m really happy they would honor me like this.”Explore more on these topicsNFLArizona CardinalsCarolina PanthersUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Niewiadoma crushes Tour de France Femmes rivals on Mont Ventoux and takes overall lead  | Tour de France Femmes | The Guardian
description: Kasia Niewiadoma took a spectacular solo victory on the legendary Mont Ventoux, securing a slim overall lead in the Tour de France Femmes after stage seven
Author: Jeremy Whittle
Headline: Kasia Niewiadoma took a spectacular solo victory on the legendary Mont Ventoux, securing a slim overall lead in the Tour de France Femmes after stage seven
Content: Kasia Niewiadoma on the podium after a devastating display of climbing on Mont Ventoux.Photograph: Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKasia Niewiadoma on the podium after a devastating display of climbing on Mont Ventoux.Photograph: Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty ImagesTour de France FemmesNiewiadoma crushes Tour de France Femmes rivals on Mont Ventoux and takes overall leadPole leaves fellow contenders behind on iconic climbDemi Vollering trails by 15sec, Marlen Reusser by 39secJeremy Whittleat Mont VentouxFri 7 Aug 2026 13.43 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 19.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKasia Niewiadoma took a spectacular solo victory on the legendary Mont Ventoux, securing a slim overall lead in theTour de France Femmesafter leaving behind her fellow race favourites Marlen Reusser and Demi Vollering.“It’s hard to describe my feelings because I’m still blown away by what just happened,” Niewiadoma,who won the yellow jersey in 2024, said of the first Tour stage victory of her career.Tour de France Femmes 2026: Kasia Niewiadoma wins on Mont Ventoux and takes yellow – liveRead moreIn one of the most memorable climbing performances on the fearsome Giant of Provence, the 31-year-old Polish rider took back the best part of two minutes on Reusser, who had led the race sinceTuesday’s individual time trial. With two stages remaining Niewiadoma leads overall by 15sec from Vollering, the 2023 champion. Reusser trails by 39sec in third after stage seven.Vollering’s initial attack, which came on one of the climb’s few hairpins, the Virage du Bois, was promptly closed down by Reusser and Niewiadoma, who, just as they had atMont Brouilly on stage five, stuck doggedly to the Dutch rider’s wheel. Their collective effort was enough to force the issue, and the trio rode ahead to contest the stage.Niewiadoma’s decisive acceleration came just under 10km from the summit, after she, Reusser and Vollering had moved ahead of the front group. Vollering and Reusser seemed more focused on each other, hesitating as Niewiadoma went clear. That sealed their fate. Since its rebirth in 2022, Niewiadoma has always finished on the podium of the Tour, and her epic duel with Vollering on Alpe d’Huez in 2024 may yet be replayed in this weekend’s racing in the hills around Nice.“It means the world to me to get the yellow jersey by winning on the Ventoux,” she said. “A lot of work went into it. Each year you have to come to the Tour even stronger than the year before because the level is going up so much.”View image in fullscreenMarlen Reusser (in yellow) and Demi Vollering pursue Kasia Niewiadoma on Mont Ventoux.Photograph: Nicolas Tucat/AFP/Getty ImagesNiewiadoma’s pace took her clear on the approach to Chalet Reynard, while Reusser and Vollering appeared to be riding through treacle. In fact, it was more of a tactical stalemate that was finally broken when Vollering attacked Reusser in the final kilometre to finish second on the stage. Reusser crossed the line in a weary fourth place but there was plenty of suffering elsewhere on a stage in which a number of big names fell by the wayside.Among those to leave even before the stage started was Anna van der Breggen of SD Worx-Protime, who dropped out on Friday morning. The 36-year-old Dutch rider, who finished second overall in the Vuelta and third in the Giro earlier this year, was described as “not feeling at her best”. “We kept hoping she would start to feel better as the race progressed, but unfortunately that improvement never came. We decided not to take any unnecessary risks and to give her the rest she needs,” said the sports director Danny Stam.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEven on the less arduous slopes, before the notoriously steep bend at Saint-Estève that signals the start of the official climb, the peloton was dramatically reduced. Multiple riders fell away as the gradient increased. Early casualties of the pacesetting included the defending champion, Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, and Kim Le Court,winner of stage six, both of whom definitively waved goodbye to any lingering thoughts of a high overall finish. Ferrand-Prévot’s Visma Lease-a-Bike teammate Femke de Vries was another who suffered as the Ventoux’s gradients bit into tired legs and the pair joined forces in a bid to limit their losses.At the front, Reusser’s Movistar team sought to control any attacks, but Vollering’s FDJ United-Suez proved equally as resilient. Noemi Rüegg made a huge effort to set the pace for the EF Education-Oatly team leader, Cédrine Kerbaol, but was eventually swept away by Vollering’s accelerations. Niewiadoma spent time training on the Ventoux in June with her husband, the former professional Taylor Phinney, saying she sold the idea to him as a “romantic getaway”.There may be little love lost, however, between Niewiadoma and her old rival Vollering in the Tour’s final 48 hours. “We have a strong team,” Niewiadoma said, “but I’m expecting a massive fight for everything – points, bonus seconds, everything – because the gap is so small.”Explore more on these topicsTour de France FemmesCyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil war | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The Mexican and Argentinian football federations have issued their public backing for beleaguered Fifa president Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Mexican and Argentinian football federations have issued their public backing for beleaguered Fifa president Gianni Infantino in a move that has deepened world football’s civil war
Content: Gianni Infantino holds the World Cup trophy alongside actor and Fifa World Cup 2026 ambassador Salma Hayek before the opening game in Mexico City.Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino holds the World Cup trophy alongside actor and Fifa World Cup 2026 ambassador Salma Hayek before the opening game in Mexico City.Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/ReutersFifaMexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil warMexico breaks ranks with Concacaf to support Fifa chiefGrowing speculation country will switch to ConmebolMatt HughesFri 7 Aug 2026 05.33 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 18.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMexico’s football federation has broken ranks with the rest of Concacaf by publicly backing the beleagueredGianni Infantinoin a move that has deepened world football’s civil war.Concacaf has called for a thorough review of Fifa’s governance in the light of the World Cup sell-off debacle, and is backing Uefa’s demands for meaningful change, although has yet to follow its European counterparts bythreatening to boycott tournamentsif they do not achieve their objectives.In a statement issued on Thursday night, the FMF went some way towards explaining Concacaf’s reticence, as its second-biggest member after the US was unequivocal in its support for the Fifa president. In a Fifa statementreleased under Infantino’s nameon Wednesday, the world governing body had called for its institutional practices to be respected, a coded way of condemning any leadership challenge before next March’s scheduled presidential election, which the FMF endorsed.Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’Read more“The Mexican Football Federation is convinced that football is its fundamental value and that its best defence lies in institutional integrity and respect for the governance and processes that safeguard it,” the FMF said. “Therefore, the FMF will not recognise or approve any process convened outside of this institutional framework, and it embraces the call issued by president Infantino on 5 August 2026 to collectively continue developing football for the benefit of its 211 member associations.“The FMF supports president Infantino’s leadership in continuing to promote the development of football through institutional strengthening.”The Argentina Football Association (AFA) followed Mexico’s lead by backing Infantino in a gushing tribute and expressing support for his leadership over the past decade. Unlike Concacaf, South America’s Conmebol appears united behind Infantino, while in an intriguing subplot there is growing speculation that Mexico would like to switch confederations to join the latter.“In relation to the recent events that are public knowledge, we must recognise the decision of the administration to withdraw a project that generated, within the football family and from its inception, many more uncertainties than certainties,” the AFA statement read.“That is why it is worth highlighting the acceptance of the errors made in this process and the apology expressed in the heartfelt message displayed to the 211 member associations ofFifa. Prioritising governance standards is a fundamental pillar for strengthening good relations between Fifa, its member associations and the confederations.“In the same way, and as we have already expressed, you are leading a management that led to a profound transformation of Fifa, which opened the doors of the organisation to all member associations and confederations, so that with a frank and direct dialogue, we can, together, continue to promote football at all levels and disciplines.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“This transformation was based on a model of transparent governance, respect for statutory structures and the monitoring of democratic procedures, essential principles for the football family to be united, firm and working to continue generating improvements in sports and institutions, which have an impact on a better quality of life for millions of human beings who practise our beloved sport.“Accordingly, with the upcoming Fifa congress approaching, the association that we proudly preside over firmly believes and reaffirms that the way forward is to continue to work under your leadership, so that we can continue to develop better and even more inclusive football.”Earlier on Thursday, the Confederation of African Football had reaffirmed its support for Infantino, providing him with further allies as he fights to extend his 10-year reign.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Vinícius Júnior and Yan Diomande are among more than 100 players at an agency owned by the hip-hop legend
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Vinícius Júnior and Yan Diomande are among more than 100 players at an agency owned by the hip-hop legend
Content: Roc Nation Sports have had to deal with two separate legal challenges over their handling of Yan Diomande, who has joined Real Madrid.Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRoc Nation Sports have had to deal with two separate legal challenges over their handling of Yan Diomande, who has joined Real Madrid.Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty ImagesTransfer windowJay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer marketVinícius Júnior and Yan Diomande are among more than 100 players at an agency owned by the hip-hop legendEd AaronsFri 7 Aug 2026 15.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from thestreaming service Tidaland his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.Arsenal hopes dashed after Vinícius Júnior extends Real Madrid contract to 2032Read moreEstablished five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, includingVinícius Júnior– the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. WhileArsenal– now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City afterBarcelona stole a marchon their great rivals.View image in fullscreenA phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports.Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/APOn the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete hisrecord £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history –was picturedwith his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.A long-running saga that began whenLiverpoolhad a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Groupinstigated proceedingsat the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and owns Leganés as part of his Blue Crow network of clubs –told the Guardian last yearDiomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowReal MadridJay-ZArsenalLiverpoolfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Chess: Adams loses first British Championship game since 1988 to rising star | Chess | The Guardian
description: The Taunton grandmaster had been unbeaten in 87 games in a row, during which time he had won all his nine titles
Author: Leonard Barden
Headline: The Taunton grandmaster had been unbeaten in 87 games in a row, during which time he had won all his nine titles
Content: Michael Adams had gone 87 games at the British Championship without defeat before losing to Svyatoslav Bazakutsa on Tuesday.Photograph: Eteri Kublashvili/FideView image in fullscreenMichael Adams had gone 87 games at the British Championship without defeat before losing to Svyatoslav Bazakutsa on Tuesday.Photograph: Eteri Kublashvili/FideLeonard Barden on chessChessChess: Adams loses first British Championship game since 1988 to rising starThe Taunton grandmaster had been unbeaten in 87 games in a row, during which time he had won all his nine titlesLeonard BardenFri 7 Aug 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Adams, the 54-year-old Taunton grandmaster aiming for a record-equalling 10th British title, began with three wins but in round four suffered his first championship defeat since 1988 when he resigned a lost rook endgame after 60 moves to the rising Ukrainian talent Svyatoslav Bazakutsa, 18, who lives in Liverpool.Adams has won nine British titles, one short of Jonathan Penrose’s record, but missed many championships in the 1990s and 2000s when he was campaigning for the world crown.View image in fullscreen4036Willy Hendriks v Jeroen Bosch, German Bundesliga 2007. White (to move) is three pawns down, so Hendriks settled for a draw by perpetual check with Qh6+ and Qg6+. Later he discovered a subtle way to win, and showed the diagram to the Dutch legend Jan Timman, who at first also declared the game drawn before changing his mind. Can you find White’s winning move?It was still a remarkable record of 87 classical British Championship games without a single defeat. The sequence included his 1989 victory, when he became the youngest ever winner at 17, a record which still stands, as well as his later triumphs in 1997, 2010, 2011, 2016, 2018 (when he won 3-1 in a playoff with Luke McShane which included a rapidplay loss), 2019, 2023 and 2025.The 108-player 2026 British Championship, with a total prize fund of £34,000, finishes on Sunday at the University of Warwick in Coventry. There is a strong youthful challenge this year. Five of the eight leaders after the fifth round were under-21s, while four of them were still under-18s.Leaders after seven of the nine rounds were Shreyas Royal 6; Adams, Harry Grieve, Bazakutsa, Simon Williams and Peter Roberson all 5.5.Royal, at 17 England’s youngest ever grandmaster, took the outright lead with animpressive victory over McShane, the top seed.If Royal goes on to win the title, it will seriously embarrass the England selectors who omitted him from the team of five for next month’s Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.The eighth and penultimate round starts at 2.30pm on Saturday. Royal’s game as Black sgainst Adams will be viewable with computer analysison lichesswith grandmaster commentaryon YouTube.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChess: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, breaks another world age record at Dole TrophyRead moreBodhana Sivanandan, 11, beat a grandmaster for the fourth time in her fledgling career in Tuesday’s fourth round and it was her most impressive victory yet, with 99% accuracy according to one computer evaluation. GM Ameet Ghasi is a seasoned performer, butSivanandan strategically outplayed himbefore finishing with the smart tactic 33…Nxe2! Immediately after her victory, Sivanandan wasinterviewed for the live commentaryby GM Nick Pert.Sivanandan’s exceptional performance in this game arguably deserves recognition as the female equivalent of Bobby Fischer’s 1956Game of the Centuryagainst Donald Byrne, played when the future world champion was 13. Fischer’s concept 17…Be6!! was grandiose, but the ensuing windmill tactics were relatively simple to calculate. Sivanandan, two years younger, used a more complex strategy to perfection.4036:1 Rg1! wins. If 1…Qd7 2 Rh3+! gxh3 3 Qh6+ Kg8 4 gxh3+ Kf7 5 Rg7+ Ke8 6 Rxd7 and wins.Explore more on these topicsChessLeonard Barden on chessnewsShareReuse this content

title: Infantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten roots | Fifa | The Guardian
description: It has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: It has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010
Content: Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell the World Cup led to a backlash which leaves him scrabbling to save his presidency.Composite: Getty, Alamy, Reuters, ShutterstockView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s plan to sell the World Cup led to a backlash which leaves him scrabbling to save his presidency.Composite: Getty, Alamy, Reuters, ShutterstockFifaInfantino’s World Cup sell-off debacle has rocked football but Fifa’s crisis has deep and rotten rootsIt has been a remarkable few days for an institution that may be irredeemable but this is a story that stretches back to a decision in 2010Jonathan WilsonFri 7 Aug 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere are decades in which nothing happens, and weeks in which decades happen, and those weeks tend to result in leaders being toppled. Not even a fortnight ago, Gianni Infantino wastaking his victory lapon Instagram, attacking “those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours” who had dared to question elements of his World Cup, which had generated a record $15bn in revenues. But the next day came the revelation of his plan to sell the World Cup to outside investors and a backlash that has him scrabbling to save his presidency.It has been a remarkable few days, but this is a story whose roots stretch way back, to the decision in Zurich in 2010 to award the 2022 World Cup not to the USbut to Qatar, to a furious Bill Clinton hurling an ashtray across the room and demanding action, to an FBI inquiry into corruption, and to the flipping of the larger-than-lifeConcacaf general secretary Chuck Blazer, who had two apartments in Trump Tower, one for himself and one for his cats.Mexico and Argentina line up behind Infantino to deepen football’s civil warRead moreBlazer now appears as the cheery, bearded, acceptable face of Fifa corruption. He drove about on a mobility scooter with his parrot, Max, on his shoulder and once high-fived Vladimir Putin after the Russian president suggested he looked like Karl Marx. But it was Blazer’s evidence that led to the arrests at Zurich’s Baur au Lac hotel in 2015 andthe resignation of Sepp Blattersix days later.The overwhelming favourite to replace Blatter was the president of Uefa, Michel Platini. He, though, was unacceptable to the US, because it was his decision to switch his vote to Qatar, following – although he maintains not as a result of – a meeting at the Élysée Palace with the then French president Nicolas Sarkozy and the crown prince and prime minister of Qatar.Conveniently, evidence was found of a payment he had received fromFifain 2011 leading to his suspension. The Berne federal prosecutor, Michael Lauber, broke protocol to name Platini as something “between a witness and a suspect”. It was enough: Platini stepped aside and Infantino stepped in as Uefa’s candidate. Lauber subsequently became attorney general of Switzerland only to resign after secretly meeting Infantino while investigating Fifa. Platini was subsequently cleared and is suing both Fifa and Infantino.View image in fullscreenChuck Blazer’s evidence led to the resignation of Sepp Blatter (left) in 2015.Photograph: Fabrice Coffrini/AFP/Getty ImagesAt the time, Infantino was the secretary general of Uefa, notable largely for his comical earnestness while conducting Champions League draws. He was elected Fifa president in February 2016, defeating the Bahraini Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation, an avid hunter of wild boar who denied allegations of complicity in the torture of pro-democracy campaigners. Key had been a late change of mind by the Caribbean bloc: Sunil Gulati, the president of the US Soccer Federation, took credit for his persuasiveness.With an ally elected, the US, Mexico and Canada won the right to host the 2026 World Cup. “You wanted to have it there and I wanted to have it there, and we really did it before we came to office,” Donald Trump, performing his classic trick of supervillain exposition, told Infantino at a dinner in Davos in 2020. The order of events is worth reiterating: Infantino was elected in February 2016, Trump was inaugurated in January 2017, the World Cup hosting decision was taken in May 2018.The US has been a constant in Infantino’s presidency. He took power at a time when the US attorney general, Loretta Lynch, was promising to swill corruption out of Fifa but in terms of decisive action that has amounted to little more than a handful of cases involving dodgy South American broadcast rights deals. In May 2019 Fifa appointed as legal representatives the US law firm Paul Weiss. A few weeks earlier Paul Weiss had named a new senior partner: the former US attorney general Lynch. The following year,she praised Fifa’s newfound “transparency and ethical behaviour”.Few would agree with her. Infantino arrived promising reform, yet within a year he was removing two leaders of Fifa’s ethics commission. The same weekend that Trump sacked James Comey as head of the FBI, in part for investigating Russian interference in US politics,Infantino fired Miguel Maduro, the chair of the governance and review committee, for blocking the re-election as a Fifa vice-president of the head of the Russian Football Union Vitaly Mutko on the grounds that as Russia’s sports minister he breached guidelines on political involvement.View image in fullscreenLoretta Lynch promised to swill out corruption from Fifa during her time as US attorney general but there was minimal decisive action.Photograph: Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty ImagesInfantino repeatedly bypassed the Fifa council, ducked the scrutiny of press conferences and came increasingly to rule by fiat. Theplan to sell off a chunk of the World Cupis just the most egregious example. Why would he keep a plan of such revolutionary significance from his senior staff? Why would he give his members 53 days to consider such a plan, offering them a cash bonus to acquiesce? Why would he undermine his own tournament with hydration breaks and a half-time show in the final? Why override disciplinary protocols so the right players will be on the field, seemingly to highlight the tournament’s commercial appeal to potential investors?The people who were in on the deal were connected to the Trump family,specifically Joshua Kushner, the brother of the president’s son-in-law. Again, questions immediately arise. Why would you sell off 21% of all future revenues for only 28% of what this World Cup made? Infantino’s relationship with Trump – awarding him the inaugural Fifa Peace Prize, appearing with him at world events, giving him a Club World Cup trophy, renting an office for Fifa in Trump Tower that is seemingly barely used – had already brought criticism.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionUefa’s robust and united response, thethreat to boycott Fifa tournaments, was evidently not anticipated. The plan is dead, at least for now. Infantino, damaged, clings on, having rallied at least some senior Fifa staff atan emergency meeting in Rabatthis week. The chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, one of the two members of the five-man inner council who voted against the plan when informed about it the day before the World Cup final, was, notably, not there. Plans toexpand the World Cup to 64 teams, rallying Infantino’s base, have been accelerated.View image in fullscreenGianni Infantino’s relationship with Donald Trump has attracted plenty of criticism.Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesLetters of support that had looked as if they would ensure Infantino a further term unopposed are being withdrawn. On Friday, perhaps impressed by the promise of the 2030 World Cup final being in Casablanca, the Confederation of African Football pledged its support,joining Mexico, Argentina, Qatar, the UAE, Lebanon, Kuwait, Bhutan and Sri Lanka in backing Infantino.Perhaps there will be an election, as scheduled, next March. Perhaps Infantino can muster a majority among Fifa’s 211 members. But Uefa has vowed to “paralyse” Fifa until he is gone. The first tournament that might be boycotted is the Under- 20 Women’s World Cup, which begins in Poland on 5 September. Poland has made significant investment in infrastructure and is keen for the tournament to go ahead as scheduled but its football federation would be unlikely to step outside the Uefa bloc.Infantino is getting his karmic kicking, but why did football take so long to rebel against Fifa? | Jonathan LiewRead moreThe politicking goes on although already the discussion seems more about who might challenge or defeat Infantino than about how to change Fifa, where clientelism has reigned since João Havelange won the 1974 presidential election. The institution itself is rotten; it may be that it is irredeemable.It’s very hard to know how genuine Infantino’s attempt to reform Fifa was, but it quickly foundered. And so Fifa’s attempt to move on from the crisis caused by the executive who rented an apartment for his cats in Trump Tower has wound up back in Trump Tower, with a president who rents an office there.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside | West Ham United | The Guardian
description: The power battle over Vanessa Gold’s shares and the David Sullivan Panorama allegations are overshadowing the start of the season in the Championship
Author: John Brewin
Headline: The power battle over Vanessa Gold’s shares and the David Sullivan Panorama allegations are overshadowing the start of the season in the Championship
Content: David Sullivan is expected to take his seat against Portsmouth in the London Stadium on Saturday.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenDavid Sullivan is expected to take his seat against Portsmouth in the London Stadium on Saturday.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersWest Ham UnitedBoardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outsideThe power battle over Vanessa Gold’s shares and the David Sullivan Panorama allegations are overshadowing the start of the season in the ChampionshipJohn BrewinFri 7 Aug 2026 09.14 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 12.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, aCarabao Cupfirst-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but willDavid Sullivanbe present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.View image in fullscreenDaniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%.Photograph: David W Černý/ReutersSullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague heroJarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.Amanda Staveley consortium set to buy Gold family’s 25.1% stake in West HamRead moreUntil his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.View image in fullscreenDavid Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April.Photograph: PA Images/AlamyThe key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales ofMateus Fernandes to Tottenhamand Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.View image in fullscreenWest Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship.Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty ImagesIn the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.Explore more on these topicsWest Ham UnitedDavid SullivanCarabao CupPortsmouthfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Lucy Bronze backs Uefa’s stance on boycotting Fifa for ‘good of the game’ | Chelsea Women | The Guardian
description: Lucy Bronze has backed Uefa’s stance on boycotting all Fifa competitions for the “good of the game” and to safeguard football for future generations
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Lucy Bronze has backed Uefa’s stance on boycotting all Fifa competitions for the “good of the game” and to safeguard football for future generations
Content: Chelsea's Lucy Bronze understands next summer’s Women’s World Cup could be affected by a Uefa boycott of Fifa tournaments.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenChelsea's Lucy Bronze understands next summer’s Women’s World Cup could be affected by a Uefa boycott of Fifa tournaments.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAChelsea WomenLucy Bronze backs Uefa’s stance on boycotting Fifa for ‘good of the game’Chelsea defender speaking in Auckland before friendlySeptember’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup under threatTom GarryFri 7 Aug 2026 07.05 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 15.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLucy Bronze has backed Uefa’s stance on boycotting all Fifa competitions for the “good of the game” and to safeguard football for future generations.On Thursday Europe’s governing body doubled down on its threat – including next summer’s Women’s World Cup – amid the furore surrounding the Fifa president Gianni Infantinoand his shelved plan for a privately funded Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.Uefa maintains World Cup boycott still stands despite Fifa’s backing for InfantinoRead more“The message that we stand by … is ‘for the good of the game’. The players who play in those competitions, the European players, we stand by our beliefs and what the right thing is for our game,” the 34-year-old Chelsea and England right-back said.Bronze was speaking before Saturday’s pre-season friendly against Auckland FC at Eden Park. She was responding to a question by theNew Zealand Heraldwhether it would be disappointing not to play in Fifa competitions.She added: “If that means boycotting competitions, then that has to happen. It’s for the future of the game and not just for me today and tomorrow, it’s for all the little girls or little boys who come after us to make sure that they’re in a good place, when the game is moving forward in decades to come, not just tomorrow.”Next summer’s tournament in Brazil could be the England defender’s fourth senior World Cup. The Lionesses have reached at least the semi-finals of her previous three. Her first global competition coincidentally came in New Zealand, when she helped England reach the semi-finals of the 2008 Under-17 Women’s World Cup.Uefa’s threat of a boycott could have an impact on September’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland which is set to get under way in under a month’s time, with England due to line up in Group B alongside Brazil, Canada and Tanzania.Meanwhile, Channel 4 has confirmed it will air the knockout stages of the Women’s African Cup of Nations live, with the quarter-finals and semi-finals to be streamed on its YouTube channel. The final to be shown live on E4. It will mark the first time that a UK broadcaster has shown the tournament live.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionElsewhere, the Football Association has appointed Sian Massey-Ellis as its new senior manager for women referees. Massey-Ellis became only the second woman to join the Premier League officials list in 2010 and has officiated at 150 top-flight matches, as well as five Women’s FA Cup finals. She was first female to officiate in a men’s FA Cup final.Explore more on these topicsChelsea WomenFifaUefaGianni InfantinoWomen's footballAuckland FCFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Norway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’ | Fifa | The Guardian
description: ‘There is no way back for him’ says the NFF president as Infantino battles for support around the world
Author: Nick Ames
Headline: ‘There is no way back for him’ says the NFF president as Infantino battles for support around the world
Content: The Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness does not see a way back for Gianni Infantino.Photograph: Amanda Pedersen Giske/EPAView image in fullscreenThe Norwegian Football Federation president Lise Klaveness does not see a way back for Gianni Infantino.Photograph: Amanda Pedersen Giske/EPAFifaNorway’s Klaveness tells Fifa president Infantino to resign: ‘There is no trust now’‘There is no way back for him,’ says NFF presidentInfantino still battling for support around the worldExclusive byNick AmesFri 7 Aug 2026 07.15 EDTFirst published on Fri 7 Aug 2026 05.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Norwegian FA will ask Gianni Infantino to resign with immediate effect after his doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.Norway is the first federation to call directly for theFifapresident to step down after a series of controversies that came to a head with the crisis engulfing his Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.The decision was made at a meeting of the Norwegian Football Federation board (NFF) on Thursday night. Norway has consistently taken a lead in efforts to scrutinise Fifa’s governance and recent events have taken any faith in its leadership beyond the point of no return.Uefa maintains World Cup boycott still stands despite Fifa’s backing for InfantinoRead more“We decided that there is no trust in Infantino now,” the NFF president, Lise Klaveness, told the Guardian. “We have been worried consistently and there has been one more step in a worrying direction every year, every part of the year. The trust is now gone for us, there is no way back for Infantino.“We’re left in a very polarised cooperation globally and, I would say, chaos. So we will ask him to resign immediately so that the global football community can look ahead and cooperate going into the future.”The NFF is expected to formally write a letter requesting Infantino’s resignation in the coming week. Norway was among a handful of countries not to back his re-election as president next March, although several European federationshave withdrawn their endorsementin the past week.“We understand that we’re one country, but it’s our position,” Klaveness said. “It’s just one step further for us. We did not vote for him in 2023 but we hoped we would support him, he was elected and the reason why we were so clear in our statements was to really give the signal that we wanted him to implement the good reforms he was part of. But he didn’t, and now we will ask him to resign.”The NFF agreed to demand a full review into the package of reforms passed upon Infantino’s ascent to the presidency in 2016, which were intended to extricate Fifa from the corruption crisis that had previously dogged the governing body. Klaveness said the investigation should ask “what was implemented, what was not, what should have been implemented and what we should also implement to make this a functioning organisation”.Norway will also formalise a fresh complaint to Fifa’s ethics committee on three fronts, taking in the FFE scandal, the award of Fifa’s peace prize to Donald Trump and theFolarin Balogun affair at the World Cup. It will attempt to bring a number of major European federations on board for its submission in an effort to further increase the pressure on Infantino.“We want the ethics committee to show their work transparently because this is a very big part of the issue,” Klaveness said. “There are all kinds of control mechanisms in place but they are not really holding the council and president accountable.”View image in fullscreenGianni Infantino leaves after attending the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations match between Malawi and Zambia in Rabat.Photograph: APIn June, the NFF wrote to the ethics committee supporting a complaint by theadvocacy group FairSquare, which centred on alleged breaches of political neutrality by Infantino. It will now make a new submission that asks for the three situations to be considered individually. “We will join them in one letter but they are very different cases and we want the ethical committee to treat them separately,” Klaveness said.The NFF is understood to have particular concerns that the timing ofInfantino’s FFE offer, which promised federations significant financial gains if accepted, may constitute an abuse of position at this proximity to a presidential election. It has also been observed that the FFE scheme, had it been passed, would have locked in commitments extending well beyond Infantino’s term.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAs with its call for Infantino to step down, Norway is the first federation to adopt a public stance regarding the peace prize or the Balogun case. Fifa’s decision to suspend the USA striker’s red card during the World Cup, meaning he was free to face Belgium in the last 16, came after Trump had called Infantino to discuss the ban.Uefa’s federations have stood together in backing a potential boycott of Fifa competitions,a stance Uefa reasserted on Thursdaydespite Infantino’s shelving of FFE. Klaveness said the move is not merely symbolic and is intended to bring swift results.“There’s no point in Uefa standing in a war position for half a year,” she said. “That would not be good at all. Now it’s crucial that we do it because global football cooperation is at stake. It’s very good to see we have strong leadership in Uefa that knows now is crunch time for this case. We cannot sell out this core of football.”The first competition in line for a boycott would be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup, which is due to start in Poland on 5 September, but Klaveness expects the continued turmoil to have been resolved by then.“I hope and think it will not come to that,” she said. “A lot of water will go under the bridge before that. But this is why we ask Infantino to resign. It’s so unstable now that it’s a matter of time. He cannot recover this and we cannot put the sport on the spot. The biggest priority is to be together with Uefa and have this strong position.”Klaveness and the NFF have held a consistent line in calling for scrutiny of Fifa’s operations since she assumed her position in March 2022. She has been vocal on human rights issues and governance standards within Fifa, criticising failings surrounding the Qatar World Cup and questioning the process that awarded Saudi Arabia the 2034 edition of the tournament.Explore more on these topicsFifaFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Real Madrid’s returning manager José Mourinho is reportedly unhappy over Barcelona’s hijack while City are ready to seal deal for Morocco star Bouaddi
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Real Madrid’s returning manager José Mourinho is reportedly unhappy over Barcelona’s hijack while City are ready to seal deal for Morocco star Bouaddi
Content: Returning to Spain? Rodri is in a three-way battle with Manchester City, Barcelona and Real Madrid.Photograph: Copa/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenReturning to Spain? Rodri is in a three-way battle with Manchester City, Barcelona and Real Madrid.Photograph: Copa/Getty ImagesTransfer windowManchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continueMourinho reportedly unhappy over Barça hijackCity ready to seal deal for Morocco star BouaddiEd AaronsFri 7 Aug 2026 10.02 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 13.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks withReal Madridbroke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new dealRead moreRodri moved to the Etihad in 2019from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.Rodri, who won the World Cup Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player last month, spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday.The Spanish champions will be without Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.City havesigned Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116mand remain in negotiations with Lille over adeal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The 25-year-old is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to not to have the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority on returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.Real have already brought in the wingerYan Diomande for £115mandMarc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, so they may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Argentinian Fernández.Crystal Palacehave confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowBarcelonaManchester CityReal MadridLilleCrystal PalacenewsShareReuse this content

title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Diego Simeone keen on move for the Spurs defender while Micky Van de Ven is expected to pen a five-year extension
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Diego Simeone keen on move for the Spurs defender while Micky Van de Ven is expected to pen a five-year extension
Content: Cristian Romero looks to have played his final game for Spurs.Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCristian Romero looks to have played his final game for Spurs.Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty ImagesTransfer windowTottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new dealSimeone keen on move for Spurs defenderVan de Ven expected to pen five-year extensionEd AaronsFri 7 Aug 2026 06.37 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 18.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTottenham are in talks withAtlético Madridover the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set tojoin Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.Football transfer rumours: Cristian Romero to leave Spurs for … Arsenal?Read moreReports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defendersJan Paul van HeckeandMarcos Senesi this summer– insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowAtlético MadridTottenham HotspurnewsShareReuse this content

title: Afcon’s biennial switch cost African governing body deal worth more than $1bn | Africa Cup of Nations | The Guardian
description: A deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial to a four-yearly event
Author: Osasu Obayiuwana
Headline: A deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial to a four-yearly event
Content: Caf has opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the next three editions of the Africa Cup of Nations.Photograph: Siphiwe Sibeko/ReutersView image in fullscreenCaf has opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the next three editions of the Africa Cup of Nations.Photograph: Siphiwe Sibeko/ReutersAfrica Cup of NationsAfcon’s biennial switch cost African governing body deal worth more than $1bnChange to four-year cycle led to abandonment of 2025 bidCaf has not had long-term financial deal since 2019Osasu ObayiuwanaFri 7 Aug 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 03.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA deal worth at least $1bn in secured income over eight years was abandoned by the Confederation of African Football (Caf) because the governing body decided to switch the Africa Cup of Nations from a biennial toa four-yearly event, the Guardian can reveal.On 5 July 2025, the eve of the delayed Women’sAfrica Cup of Nationsin Morocco, the Caf president, Patrice Motsepe, told the Guardian in Rabat, after a prolonged discussion of the bidding process at an executive committee meeting, that a decision on a winning bid would be made “in due course”.Plan to expand Africa Cup of Nations from 24 to 28 teams is rejectedRead more“We announced in Addis Ababa this $1bn partnership that we are looking at over the next eight years. There is a lot of good progress that has been made,” he said.On 23 July, four days after the World Cup final in New York, Caf opened a fresh tender for the marketing and commercial rights of the 2028, 2032 and 2036 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) tournaments, with bidders given until 24 August to hand in their bid books.The tender is in complete contrast to the 2025 bidding round, in which the entirety of Caf’s competition portfolio was bundled for sale.Luxolo September, Caf’s head of communications, confirmed that the change in Afcon frequency is wholly responsible for the abandonment of the 2025 bidding round that was on the verge of completion.“As foreshadowed by the president in his comments last year, following the receipt and evaluation of bids and presentations from the bidders, in the second half of 2025, Caf entered into detailed discussions with shortlisted bidders regarding the precise terms and conditions of their proposals.“However, at its meeting on 20 December 2025, the Caf executive committee took a unanimous decision – in the interest of African football – to move the Afcon to a four-year cycle, bringing the competition into alignment with the international match calendar,” September said. “This was a significant decision for African football. That executive committee decision materially changed the scope of the commercial rights available for tender, with the result that the 2025 ITT (Invitation To Tender) process could no longer proceed in its existing form.”View image in fullscreenPatrice Motsepe (left) said in 2025 that ‘good progress’ was being made over a $1bn deal for Caf.Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty ImagesIt has been seven years since Caf has had a long-term deal to secure its financial future. The 2016-2028 billion-dollar “minimum guarantee” revenue contract that it signed with the French company Lagardère during the tenure of Issa Hayatou, the late Cameroonian president of Caf, was the first of its kind for the organisation.“The Memorandum of Understanding with Lagardère was agreed by a team I led with Hicham [El Amrani, then Caf general secretary] in May 2015, in Zurich,” Suketu Patel, then chair of Caf’s finance committee, said in 2019.“On that same day, we met with Infront. Their indicative offer on the table was a $450m minimum guarantee for eight years, as opposed to the $1bn, for 12 years, from Lagardère.“If you look at our earlier contract of 2009, we had a minimum guarantee of $150m, but our income for the period was actually around $350m. We anticipated that the 12-year contract would have yielded about $1.3bn.“I can tell you that whilst President Hayatou and I had differences on political matters, we never had one on the management of Caf finances. He did not interfere with the processes established for good governance.”But that agreement was unilaterally terminated in December 2019 during the tenure of Ahmad Ahmad, Hayatou’s successor as Caf president.A protracted legal dispute at the International Chamber of Commerce led to Caf, just over a year into the presidency of Motsepe, paying Lagardère a final settlement of $50m, as compensation for the breach of contract, just before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.“There is no way that any sponsor will be prepared to pay the same amount of money for a deal in which you would normally have four Afcons over an eight-year period, when you will now only have two. That is certainly a no-brainer,” said a former FA president with expertise in financial matters.Explore more on these topicsAfrica Cup of NationsFootball politicsFifanewsShareReuse this content

title: Leeds extend lead at top of Super League after thrilling late win at Wakefield | Super League | The Guardian
description: Chris Hankinson’s late try helped Leeds hit back from 16-0 down to beat second-placed Wakefield 24-22 in a Super League classic
Author: Aaron Bower
Headline: Chris Hankinson’s late try helped Leeds hit back from 16-0 down to beat second-placed Wakefield 24-22 in a Super League classic
Content: Chris Hankinson touches down three minutes from time to complete Leeds’ comeback.Photograph: Alex Whitehead/SWpix.com/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenChris Hankinson touches down three minutes from time to complete Leeds’ comeback.Photograph: Alex Whitehead/SWpix.com/ShutterstockSuper LeagueLeeds extend lead at top of Super League after thrilling late win at WakefieldWakefield 22-24 LeedsHankinson’s try seals victory after 16-point deficitAaron Bowerat DIY Kitchens StadiumFri 7 Aug 2026 17.12 EDTLast modified on Fri 7 Aug 2026 19.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWhisper it but perhaps that was the performance of a champion side. All week the talk had been aboutWakefield Trinityand whether this could be the night they declared themselves as a Super League force in front of a sell-out crowd against Leeds Rhinos.In the end, they probably did that, despite the result. These two West Yorkshire rivals served up a classic under the Belle Vue lights but in the end, despite never leading until the 77th minute, Leeds mustered up all their strength and championship credentials to complete a comeback which began when they trailed by 16 points with half an hour left.Super League closes in on gamechanging investment from Australia’s NRLRead moreAt that stage it felt inevitable that Wakefield would be going joint-top of the table with Leeds. Trinity, a Championship side two years ago, looked as though they were about to deliver their biggest statement yet that they could be about to end their 60-year wait for a major trophy. However, the Rhinos dug deep and found a way.James McDonnell’s try gave them hope before three minutes later Cameron Smith, the game’s outstanding player who will play for Wakefield in 2027, scored to mean a 22-6 lead for Wakefield had suddenly been reduced to 22-18. As it entered the championship rounds, it was Trinity who blinked, as Chris Hankinson seized on a Jake Connor kick, with Connor converting to win it.This was a result and a performance born out of Leeds and Brad Arthur’s darkest moment together. Last year they were beaten in the final seconds by St Helens in the playoffs and the Rhinos spent all pre-season warning there would be no repeat. This felt like living proof of that; Leeds showing they can go to the well in the toughest of times to secure a huge win.“That’s the evidence of us learning from it,” Arthur said. “We’ve done the work. Under a bit of pressure we kept our composure, our key players kept composure. I challenged them at half-time to go right to the 80th minute … boy, they did it.” Leeds were outplayed for large stretches here, with Wakefield good value for their 16-6 half-time lead.Tries from Isaiah Vagana, Caleb Hamlin-Uele and Jayden Myers put Trinity in control, and had the majority of this sell-out crowd dreaming of going joint-top. Brodie Croft’s try just before the break gave Leeds hope but when Jack Sinfield scored against his former club to make it 22-6, it looked as though the momentum was back with Wakefield.The Rhinos were on the ropes. But this group are built differently in 2026, with McDonnell’s try starting the comeback and Hankinson’s finishing it – with Leeds surviving a frantic final few moments to go four points clear with five games left. With this win Leeds are now heavy favourites to finish top, which would result in their first piece of silverware in six years.As for Wakefield, they will be bruised by this. Having lost by four to Wigan in the cup quarter-finals and now by two here to the league leaders, this was perhaps a subtle lesson again about the final step they still have to take. They should, however, take great pride from this – and great heart from what they did for the most part if they meet Leeds again in the playoffs.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“The story this year is not over,” Wakefield’s coach, Daryl Powell, said. “Leeds might have got off tonight but I’m pretty comfortable going against them again in a playoff game. They’re a great side but I watched us thinking if we play how we did in the first half we’re a fair team to defend against and play against.”One thing is for certain: if these two meet again under the lights at Old Trafford in eight weeks and serve up a repeat of this classic, nobody will be complaining.Explore more on these topicsSuper LeagueWakefield TrinityLeeds RhinosRugby leaguenewsShareReuse this content

title: Andrew Flintoff makes surprise exit as England Lions head coach after two years | Andrew Flintoff | The Guardian
description: Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of England Lions, saying he has taken great pride in seeing ‘the best young cricketers in the country’ develop
Author: Ali Martin
Headline: Andrew Flintoff has stepped down as head coach of England Lions, saying he has taken great pride in seeing ‘the best young cricketers in the country’ develop
Content: Andrew Flintoff has been head coach of the England Lions since September 2024.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAndrew Flintoff has been head coach of the England Lions since September 2024.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesAndrew FlintoffAndrew Flintoff makes surprise exit as England Lions head coach after two yearsOther demands meant he was unable to commit fullyMike Yardy will step in for upcoming Pakistan fixtureAli MartinFri 7 Aug 2026 14.15 EDTFirst published on Fri 7 Aug 2026 13.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndrew Flintoff has decided to step down as the head coach of England Lions with immediate effect before his winter spell working in Australia’s Big Bash League (BBL).The former all-rounder, 48, has been in charge of England’s second string since September 2024 and had been given the all-clear to leave this winter’s Lions tour of South Africa early to take up his new role at BBL side Sydney Thunder.But the England and WalesCricketBoard announced on Friday evening that Flintoff has left the role. He is said to have decided the BBL job – plus TV work and family commitments – means he cannot commit fully to the Lions.Dazn buys Australia series rights as platforms jostle over England white-ball tourRead moreIn an ECB statement, Flintoff said: “Unfortunately I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.”Flintoff’s departure is somewhat abrupt, with Rob Key, the England men’s team director, having moved to defend his former teammate and close friend last week amid recent criticism of his role with the Lions team.“We’ve been incredibly fortunate to have him do it,” said Key. “I thought it was disrespectful for people to say that he shouldn’t have been doing it. He’s been outstanding in that job, and we’ve been incredibly fortunate to have him.”Flintoff had recently been negotiating with the counties over player availability for the quasi-Lions XI that will serve as warm-up opposition for Pakistan’s Test squad in a four-day match at Beckenham starting on Wednesday.Mike Yardy, the head coach of England Under-19s, will now run that team – officially the Professional County Club Select XI – using young players not currently in the Hundred or not required by their counties in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMeanwhile, England’s senior squad to face Pakistan in the first Test at Headingley, which starts on 19 August, has suffered an injury doubt, with the opener Emilio Gay having retired hurt while batting for Durham an apparent shoulder problem. Ollie Pope, a middle order player, is currently the reserve batter in the squad and so a full-time opener may have to be called up if Gay’s injury proves significant.Explore more on these topicsAndrew FlintoffEngland cricket teamCricketnewsShareReuse this content
